definitions.explanation: A literary or formal way to say 'many' or 'numerous,' emphasizing a large but unspecified number of things. Conveys a sense of weight and significance, often used when looking back on experiences or challenges.

examples.japanese: {幾多|いくた}の{困難|こんなん}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えた。
{幾多|いくた}の{試練|しれん}を{経|へ}て、{彼|かれ}は{強|つよ}くなった。
examples.english: Through countless trials, he became stronger.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{幾多|いくた}の{自然|しぜん}{災害|さいがい}に{見舞|みま}われながらも、そのたびに{復興|ふっこう}してきた。
examples.english: This region has been hit by numerous natural disasters, yet it has recovered each time.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary and somewhat elevated expression. Typically modifies nouns related to hardship, experience, or significance: {困難|こんなん} (difficulties), {試練|しれん} (trials), {犠牲|ぎせい} (sacrifices), {経験|けいけん} (experiences).
More formal and literary than {数多|かずおお}くの or たくさんの. Rarely used in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幾多|いくた}の{困難|こんなん} (numerous difficulties)
- {幾多|いくた}の{試練|しれん} (countless trials)
- {幾多|いくた}の{犠牲|ぎせい} (many sacrifices)
- {幾多|いくた}の{変遷|へんせん} (many changes/transitions)
